purpose: Post-Validation-16 fix (starting commit 53f72d2). Answers, per flagged id: what visual cues MUST be present so a viewer identifies THIS hobby rather than a visually-adjacent one (positive_anchors), and what nearby concept must the scene NOT accidentally become (anti_confusions). Applied via id-exact overrides in object_first_rules_v2.json routing to dedicated containment rules in structural_containment_rules_v2.json whose scene_template embeds these anchors directly, since generic archetype-level grammar was proven by real visual QA to be too broad for these 5 ids.
authoritative_visual_findings_source: ChatGPT visual review of the paid Validation-16 batch, commit 53f72d2 - supplied as authoritative input, never re-derived by Claude, no image opened this checkpoint.

transport.modelrailways.validation16_finding: SUBSTANTIVE FAIL - image read as a full-size real steam railway in a city, not a model railway. Scale identity was lost.
positive_anchors: a tabletop model-railway layout, not a real railway
a miniature train on tiny-scale tracks
miniature buildings and miniature trees/scenery built at model scale
a visible model-layout base, baseboard, or tabletop edge framing the whole scene
scale-model terrain construction (foam, plaster, or scenic-ground texture typical of a diorama)
an intentionally crafted diorama appearance, not a photographed real place
hobby tools (small paintbrush, glue, scenic scatter material) resting nearby as scale cues
a deliberate size contrast where the miniature buildings/trees read as small relative to the framing
anti_confusions: real urban transit or a real train station
photographic railway photography of an actual place

media.anime.validation16_finding: SUBSTANTIVE FAIL - read as an empty convention/presentation hall with aurora-like screen content plus pseudo-Japanese text; did not communicate anime specifically.
positive_anchors: original, unbranded anime-style figurines clearly visible as small physical collectible objects on a shelf or desk
animation cels or storyboard/key-frame sheets as physical printed objects
acrylic-style collectible display stands with original, generic (non-copyrighted) character silhouette designs
manga/anime-style art books with blank or unreadable covers
an animation light table or light box as a physical prop
frame strips or cel layers stacked or fanned out

vivid, original, clearly Japanese-animation-styled illustrated imagery (fantasy/mecha/creature) rendered AS printed artwork, a cel, or a figurine - never as a physically-present human character in the scene
a monitor or screen (if present) showing clearly stylized ORIGINAL animation-style imagery with no real human figure on it
anti_confusions: a generic conference hall or presentation venue
a generic cinema (that is media.movies' territory, not anime's)
an aurora/abstract light show with no anime-specific object present
general illustration or fine art with no anime-specific stylistic or object cue
any recognizable copyrighted franchise character, and any pseudo-Japanese or Japanese-look-alike decorative lettering used as filler text

business.startups.validation16_finding: MINOR - collapsed into an electronics maker/prototyping-workshop reading, too narrow for the broader concept of an early-stage company.
positive_anchors: an early-stage product prototype (not limited to electronics - could be physical goods, packaging, or a service-adjacent physical artifact)
planning artifacts (blank/abstract sticky notes, index cards, a whiteboard with only abstract non-legible marks)
a launch/preparation environment feel - boxes ready to ship, a small stack of packaging mockups, a product sitting mid-iteration
multiple distinct prototype iterations or categories side by side, suggesting experimentation rather than one single engineering bench
small-team workspace traces (a couple of distinct desk setups, not one lone maker's bench)
a general sense of 'early-stage company building and iterating on something', not 'hobbyist electronics tinkering'
anti_confusions: a pure electronics/maker prototyping hobby scene (that is technology's/physical_prototype's territory, not startups')
a readable pitch deck, slide, or any legible business-plan text

music.pop.validation16_finding: MINOR - read as vinyl collecting / hi-fi listening / general music appreciation rather than specifically pop music.
positive_anchors: bold, saturated stage-light color language (magenta/cyan/gold stage-wash gels, not a warm vinyl-lounge glow)
a polished, commercial pop-production environment feel
a studio microphone shown purely as an object (on a stand, not held)
synth pads, a mixing controller, or other music-production tools as supporting objects
bright, graphic, high-energy lighting rather than a cozy amber listening-room mood
vinyl/CD/cassette elements allowed only as small supporting objects, never as the dominant hero
a rhythmic, commercial, high-energy visual feel distinct from an intimate listening ritual
anti_confusions: vinyl collecting as the dominant subject (that is a distinct, already-validated sibling concept, not pop music)
any recognizable singer, celebrity likeness, copyrighted album artwork, or band logo

learning.mock_trial.validation16_finding: MINOR - read as general legal practice / case preparation rather than specifically a mock trial simulation.
positive_anchors: an educational/simulation courtroom setup, distinctly staged for practice rather than a real proceeding
clearly arranged, mirrored prosecution and defense tables facing each other
an empty witness stand as a distinct visible element
practice/training-style evidence exhibits (labeled generically as practice materials, not real case evidence)
training or rehearsal cues - a stopwatch, a scoring rubric sheet with only abstract non-legible marks, or a 'practice round' feel
a school or training-facility architectural feel rather than a working law firm or real courthouse
anti_confusions: ordinary legal practice or real case preparation (that is legal_practice's default territory for other ids, not mock trial specifically)
an oversized generic gavel used as the sole subject (a stock-art cliche explicitly to avoid)
any readable, invented real-sounding case name
